title: CS Daily Scratchpad — Harper Gomez — 2026-06-30
content:
Daily scratchpad — goals for 2026-06-30

Top priorities:
- ACME Corp QBR prep (10:00 AM PT) — main focus
- Renewal: ACME annual renewal due 2026-07-15 — finalize pricing + SOW
- Support follow-ups: two P1 tickets, one demo request from product team

QBR (10:00 AM) — attendees: Alex Chen (SE), Jordan Lee (AE), Maya Singh (Customer Exec), Harper Gomez (CS)
- Pre-read sent? yes (shared) — confirm Alex added perf slides
- Deck: 12 slides: executive summary, adoption metrics, cost per 1k tokens, latency SLOs, recent incidents, roadmap fit, recommended next steps
- Talking points:
  * Usage growth: +28% QoQ driven by search reranker and chat assistant
  * Cost breakdown: batching + quantization saved ~22% (see sheet)
  * Reliability: 99.93% last 90d; two small incidents in May (root cause: cold cache on region us-west2)
  * Ask for exec sponsorship for Dedicated pilot (2x A100s) for predictable latency
- Prep checklist:
  - [x] Finalize deck cover + exec summary
  - [ ] Confirm SE demo config (Jordan to validate GPU quota) — action: Jordan (due EOD 6/30)
  - [ ] Run latest usage query and add top-10 routes by tokens (Harper) — action: Harper (due 9:00 AM 6/30)
  - [ ] Update renewal proposal with 10% volume discount tier (Alex)
  - [ ] Send meeting calendar + dial-in to execs (Harper)
- Parking lot: cost optimization case study for their search pipeline (follow post-QBR)

Renewal timeline:
- Contract renewal date: 2026-07-15
- Current ARR: $420k/year
- Expansion opportunity: add Redwood Optimize + Dedicated pilot (~$120k ARR incremental)
- Next steps:
  * Draft SOW + pricing options (3 tiers) — status: draft started
  * Internal pricing approval (ops) — blocker: confirm Dedicated capacity pricing (ping finance)
  * Renewal check-in call w/ AE next week (Jordan to schedule)

Support follow-ups:
- P1-9876 (search latency regression) — owner: Alex Chen — update: mitigated via temporary routing; need long-term fix (KV cache tuning). Action: file PR for config changes, link: JIRA-CS-9876
- P2-9911 (embedding mismatch on reranker) — owner: Nina Patel — currently investigating dataset drift
- Demo request: product team wants 15-min deep-dive on function calling + structured outputs — schedule after QBR; need SE to prepare demo snippet (Jordan)

Notes / talking points for QBR:
- Show concrete before/after numbers when we enabled prefix caching on their top route (latency down ~40%)
- Emphasize operational guarantees with Dedicated (predictable throughput) and rollback policies for rollouts
- Risk: if they delay commit beyond 7/15, price increase may apply; mention gently

Open questions to surface in meeting:
- Are there any plans to migrate sensitive workloads on-prem? (if yes -> discuss Redwood Private)
- Will they commit to multi-quarter usage targets for discount tier?
- Which internal stakeholders own platform budget (finance vs infra)?

Personal to-dos (today):
- 08:45 — run usage query and paste top 10 routes into slide 4 (Harper)
- 09:30 — quick sync with Alex to confirm perf numbers
- 10:00 — QBR w/ ACME (deliver talk track + handoff to SE)
- 13:00 — update renewal doc + upload to confluence
- 15:00 — follow up on P1-9876 PR status
- End of day — send summary email to ACME + internal recap to AE/SE

Quick links:
- ACME QBR confluence: confluence://pages/ACME-QBR-2026
- Usage sheet: sheets://redwood/usage-trends-acme-2026
- Slack thread: slack://thread/CH1J2K3/customer-acme-qbr

Random notes / scratch ideas:
- Consider a short one-pager on "Cost vs Latency tradeoffs" with 3 recommendations they can test in 30d (batching thresholds, quant profiles, prefix caching)
- If they opt for Dedicated, propose a 60-day pilot with success criteria: avg p95 latency < 250ms, token cost < $0.006/token

End of day reflection (placeholder)
- Wins: got exec on the QBR invite, deck shaping up
- Risks: finance pricing still outstanding
